name: Aprameya Engineering Limited
sector: Healthcare equipment distribution and turnkey hospital infrastructure
identity_note: NSE Emerge listed August 1, 2024; current SM shares and lot reconciled to audited capital. The predecessor partnership and new 70%-owned subsidiary are scoped separately.
summary: Aprameya is a hospital-equipment distributor and turnkey infrastructure integrator attempting a move into devices through a 70%-owned subsidiary. The decisive strength is real installation experience and the FY2026 collection-led debt reduction. The decisive risk is that lumpy government projects and extended customer credit have not produced durable owner cash: five-year CFO/PAT remains negative. This is a conditional recovery/new-business thesis, not an established compounder. At the October 19 close of ₹86.50, the funded base returns 7.66% against a 15% hurdle; BQS 4.20 and IAS 2.85 imply weak setup / value-trap risk. Better collection, renewed device rights and costed commissioning could change the business case; a lower price alone would not establish quality.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Aprameya Engineering Limited, ISIN INE0LQG01010, NSE Emerge APRAMEYA. Listed August 1, 2024; 19,040,000 current shares and ₹86.50 close imply ₹164.696 crore market value. Analysis cutoff October 20, 2026; no later interim financial result is assumed. Accounts use Ind AS. History includes the predecessor partnership, later standalone company and first consolidatedFY2026 accounts with Aprameya Medtech incorporated October 4, 2025. Parent holds 70%; two founders hold 15% each. The investor horizon is October 19, 2031, nominal pre-investor-tax hurdle 15%, illustrative liquidity position ₹5 lakh.

G1 Integrity: Conditional. Reviewed controls, related transactions and audit reports do not substantiate serious minority abuse. High compensation and direct founder ownership in the subsidiary require continued commercial benchmarking; statutory delays and provider recovery are precisely scoped.

G2 Reliability: Conditional. Audited parent/group/subsidiary statements reconcile after visual correction of extraction errors. Restatement differences are bounded and separated. Ageing, bank return differences and the provider claim are not declared resolved, but stress tests do not undermine the aggregate source hierarchy. A material new contradiction would require IAS NS.

G3 Funding: Conditional. Annual paths fund current claims, capital and WC through operating cash, disclosed facility caps and explicit hypothetical equity if needed. Full factory cost, loan draw conditions and monthly funding timing remain estimates. Subsidiary minority and guarantee claims are modeled, not omitted.

G4 Tradability: Conditional. Sixty observed traded sessions and 500-share lot support a conditional reference-position test. Thin sessions, active concentration caution and unobserved executable spread/depth prevent a guaranteed-exit conclusion.

Confidence is Medium in audited historical inputs, source hierarchy, governance and valuation inputs. Exact project cost and future collections are estimates with wide forecast uncertainty, not facts promoted to High confidence. The scoped financial sensitivities support conditional numerical scoring rather than a generic perfection-based hold.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS raw/final 4.20; GQS raw/final 4.60; IAS raw/final 2.85. Coverage 100% means all canonical factors are supported and scored, not that every fact is known. GQS has a non-binding ceiling of 5 because recurring CASH 3; no other override applies. Displayed one-decimal scores are 4.2/4.6/2.9, with unrounded scores retained for classification.

BQS = 0.20×4 +0.20×4 +0.12×6 +0.10×5 +0.12×3 +0.10×3 +0.08×6 +0.08×3 =4.20.
GQS = 0.40×6 +0.20×5 +0.15×3 +0.15×3 +0.10×3 =4.60.
IAS = 0.25×4.20 +0.35×2 +0.20×2 +0.10×3 +0.10×4 =2.85. GQS means Growth Quality.

GOV: 4/10, Medium. Audited controls and explicit disclosures are useful, but founder remuneration absorbs 72.2% of owner PAT and founders personally own 30% of the growth subsidiary. Funding and commercial terms require minority scrutiny. This is a stewardship discount, not a finding of unlawful compensation or diversion. Evidence: GOV, LEGAL.

MOAT: 4/10, Medium. Installation experience and OEM access help tender qualification. Technology is largely supplied by others, bids are competitive, one customer contributes 61.22%, and the new exclusive agreement renews annually. These do not establish durable pricing power. Evidence: RUNWAY, WC.

REV: 6/10, Medium. The preselected five-year parent revenue window gives 16.12% CAGR, starting at 7. A one-point adjustment reflects the lumpy and deteriorating recent trajectory: three declines in the last four annual comparisons and 59.7% parent contraction in FY2026, despite strong first-half growth. Three-year decline and the FY2022 peak are shown, not selectively substituted for the preferred window. No further small-base or TAM adjustment is added. Evidence: HIST.

DUR: 5/10, Medium. Hospital infrastructure and maintenance offer a real market, with named geographic access and a new device channel. Bid-to-order conversion, customer budgets, annual OEM renewal and factory qualification remain constraints. National spending is not secured company revenue. Evidence: RUNWAY.

CAP: 3/10, Medium. Latest normalized return on average committed operating capital is 8.70% and three-year incremental return 3.71%, below the 13–17% analytical range. FY2025 was much stronger, so this is weak cycle-level economics rather than a claim that every project destroys value. The new manufacturing investment has no demonstrated cohort return. Evidence: CAP.

CASH: 3/10, Medium. Four of the last five years have negative CFO and cumulative five-year CFO/PAT is negative. FY2026 collection is genuine improvement, but old ageing, low after-interest realization and collateral demands mean the weakness is recurring rather than a single growth-capex event. Evidence: CASH, WC.

BAL: 6/10, Medium. Debt fell to 7.136 crore and dated credit access supports core modeled cash needs. However almost all reported bank deposits are collateral, parent free cash is very small at March, and the subsidiary guarantee and asset recoverability matter. The score does not assume all bank balances are distributable. Evidence: FINANCE, MODEL.

EXEC: 3/10, Medium. The older growth narrative has not translated into steady delivery:FY2026 sales contracted sharply andH2 profitability weakened. Collection normalization is a positive outcome, while the new facility, new-product commercialization and 300–350 crore aspirational order book remain unproven. This factor is about delivery against commitments, not a second cash-flow penalty. Evidence: HIST, RUNWAY.

EARN: 3/10, Medium. Owner PAT falls from 16.1161 to 5.102 crore, and the stronger first half was followed by a loss-making parent second half. Other income is not the main explanation; fixed overheads, business volume and credit provisions matter. A recovery is possible but is not already visible in comparable full-year earnings. Evidence: HIST.

R: 2/10, Medium. The supported conditional base 7.6575% is 7.3425 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, exactly in R2. The lower-spend sensitivity barely crosses the 8% R3 boundary; that is model sensitivity, not a precise economic distinction. Evidence: MODEL.

D: 2/10, Medium. Bear terminal price 17.70 is about 79.5% below entry; severe terminal equity is exhausted even without assumed cash default. Low opening debt does not protect against stranded working capital, weaker margins and minority/loan recovery priority. Evidence: MODEL.

P: 3/10, Medium. At the base funded path,15% requires a 17.49-times parent terminal NOPAT multiple instead of 12, or materially better operating/cash assumptions. Fixed-price issuance makes a pure growth route extremely dilution-heavy. The price is not supported by the conservative recovery path, although the strong bull is possible. Evidence: MODEL.

L: 4/10, Medium. A 6.45-day theoretical exit starts in L5–6; use 5 then reduce one point for fewer-than 100-PAN caution, thin individual sessions, volatile high-low ranges and unobserved live depth. All 60 sessions actually traded; the generic SME caution is not misrepresented as zero-volume days. Evidence: LIQ.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The core business procures equipment and coordinates turnkey ICUs, NICUs, modular operating theatres, medical gas systems and related installations. Revenue is recognized on contractual delivery/acceptance rather than a subscription stream. Government hospitals and medical colleges dominate; administrative approvals, installation milestones and retentions can separate accounting sales from collection.

FY2026 revenue comprises traded goods ₹10.6060 crore, project supplies ₹42.1654 crore, business-support services ₹1.2261 crore and maintenance ₹1.1339 crore. Maintenance is only about 2.1% of sales, not yet a large recurring-profit base. The segment disclosure combines services with turnkey activity; its contribution figures exclude substantial unallocated expenses and are not enterprise EBIT margins. One customer contributes 61.22% of group revenue versus 83.05% in FY2025. All reported revenue is domestic.

The new subsidiary has only ₹0.3839 crore initial-period revenue and ₹0.0870 crore PAT. SonoScape distribution and a planned 45,000-square-foot facility introduce different product, regulatory and inventory risks. These are not simply more of the existing tender book, and 30% of the subsidiary residual economics belongs to founders outside the listed parent.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Experience installing critical-care systems, service staff and OEM relationships help meet qualification and coordination requirements. However the company largely integrates technology owned by suppliers; tender bidding, alternative dealers and direct OEM selling constrain pricing power. Customer concentration and long payment cycles can transfer more bargaining power to buyers than to the integrator.

The June SonoScape disclosure names exclusive MIS sales territories across western and southern India, but the agreement runs only toMarch 31, 2027 with annual renewal. No consideration is disclosed. Its broader product-marketing wording does not establish that every product has permanent exclusive rights. The agreement is not a manufacturing licence or proof of commercial production.

Trivitron’s own critical-care brochure shows a competing portfolio, manufacturing capability and distribution network. It is an operating comparator, not a matched public-market valuation peer. The 2024 prospectus itself found no listed Indian company with a sufficiently similar business. No current premium is justified by comparing Aprameya mechanically with high-margin medical-device IP owners or hospital operators.

The Health Ministry’sMarch 2026 PM-ABHIM update supports an infrastructure opportunity but also explicitly describes land, procurement and approval bottlenecks. Scheme spending includes civil works and public-health systems beyond Aprameya’s accessible equipment share. It is not the company’s TAM, backlog or market share.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue in ₹ crore: FY2020 12.2324; FY2021 25.9316; FY2022 199.9946; FY2023 78.1191; FY2024 65.1623; FY2025 135.7071; FY2026 group 55.1314 and parent 54.7475. TheFY2020–21 predecessor restatement is separately identified; later RHP/statutory series take precedence where overlapping. Annual additions from FY2021 onward are+13.6992,+174.0630,−121.8755,−12.9568,+70.5448 and−80.5757 crore.

The preferred five-year comparable parent CAGR is 16.12%, versus 16.28% on group revenue. Three-year group CAGR is −10.97%; four-year CAGR from the FY2022 peak is −27.54%. Reporting only the positive five-year endpoint would hide the cycle, but choosing the worst shorter window for the mechanical factor would also violate consistency. REV starts at 7 and has one explicit trajectory adjustment to 6, not an unrestricted penalty.

Turnkey/service segment sales fall from ₹125.0401 to ₹44.5254 crore while trading is almost flat at ₹10.6670/10.6060 crore. The small subsidiary adds only ₹0.3839 crore; it cannot explain the collapse or conceal it as acquisition growth. A price/volume bridge for equipment units is not disclosed. The economic cross-check is completed project revenue, customer concentration and receivable collection, not a claimed market-share percentage.

The November presentation showed strong H1 FY2026 parent sales around ₹42.14 crore and PAT ₹6.76 crore. Full parent results imply only about ₹12.61 crore second-half sales and a ₹1.72 crore second-half loss, with rounding from the presentation. That is a material reversal, not a full-year continuation of the first-half growth rate.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There are three plausible demand routes: replenished public hospital tenders, private-hospital/OEM distribution and new device manufacturing. Their probabilities and cash requirements differ. The November target of ₹300–350 crore order book over three years and May ₹190 crore bids are aspirations/pipeline, not secured orders. The datedSeptember 2025 dialysis order of ₹16.4 crore is not assumed still entirely unexecuted inOctober 2026. A current customer-by-customer backlog bridge is missing.

The base uses parent annual sales ₹80/95/110/125/140/150 crore and subsidiary ₹3/6/10/15/20/24 crore. This is an estimated recovery, below the old parent peak, not guidance. Parent EBIT margin 15% is below recent normalized margins; subsidiary grows from 10% to 14%. Parent broad operating WC 65% of sales is close toFY2025 economics but assumes better collection than the depressedFY2026 ratio. A 90% case reduces annual return to about 2.46%.

The ₹10 crore new facility budget is a scenario estimate, phased between parent building and subsidiary equipment, plus ₹1.6497 crore existing advances transferred without another cash payment. Alternatives ₹4 crore and ₹20 crore explicitly bound the uncosted plan. Maintenance remains additional at 1% of parent and 4% of subsidiary sales; long-lived buildings are not automatically replaced after five years.

Historical committed capital rose from ₹48.71 crore in FY2023 to ₹73.91 crore in FY2026 despite the latest collection release. Normalized latest ROIC is 8.70% and three-year incremental return 3.71%, below an analytical 13–17% operating capital-cost range, separate from the 15% equity hurdle. The highFY2025 earnings year is contrary evidence, but does not establish repeatable new-project returns. GQS 4.60 therefore does not award a premium merely for a new factory or a large healthcare market.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
TheMarch 2026 capital note implies promoter/group ownership about 74.05%; the two founders together hold 73.00%. A latest independently verified pledge quantity is not asserted. Director remuneration was ₹11.25/4.14/2.25/4.24/3.682 crore in FY2022–26. The latest total is 72.2% of owner PAT, although it declined with weaker business. It is included in other expenses, so comparing it only with the payroll line would create a false discrepancy. A high economic burden is not by itself unlawful remuneration. Related rent, interest and CSR payments are disclosed.

The listed parent owns 70% of Aprameya Medtech; the founders each own 15% directly. August shareholders approved an annual related-transaction ceiling of ₹50 crore. That is permission, not evidence ₹50 crore was transferred or spent. The relevant question is whether financing, asset ownership, rent and technology benefits are shared fairly. The model uses interest-bearing parent loans and 30% minority residual value, not a free transfer of listed-company cash to private holders.

Auditors report GST and TDS payment delays, including ₹4.2831 crore September GST delayed 31 days, with no undisputed dues older than six months at year-end. Small disputed income-tax/TDS demands total ₹0.0305 crore. A blocked ₹1.0722 crore input-tax credit was reversed; a ₹1.3049 crore provider recovery including paid interest remains in other assets, with a legal notice disclosed. The analysis does not allege fraudulent credit or intentional misconduct. Base gives this claim no cash recovery and tests full recovery separately.

Bank submissions differ from books, includingMarch gross receivables higher by ₹1.6275 crore and payables higher by ₹0.6366 crore. Management cites late TDS/GST-TDS booking and debit-note provisioning. These are disclosed timing/classification explanations, not independent proof that every difference is cleared. The olderFY2024 audit-trail limitation is followed byFY2026 auditor evidence of preserved logs since May 23, 2024; it is not labeled a continuing absence of controls.

Promises versus delivery:FY2025 growth andFY2026 collection/debt reduction are verified; the November 20–25% CAGR narrative was followed by a severe full-year contraction; new product/plant targets remain under implementation; June regional sales rights are real but expire unless renewed. A clean audit opinion and July SDD certificates do not eliminate these commercial and allocation risks.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical ₹ crore, FY2022 / FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 / FY2026:
Revenue: 199.9946 / 78.1191 / 65.1623 / 135.7071 / 55.1314.
Group or standalone PAT as applicable: 16.6191 / 5.3692 / 3.4907 / 16.1161 / 5.1281; FY2026 owner PAT is 5.1020.
Reported CFO: −0.3680 / −13.4904 / −9.9749 / −10.6353 / 31.2332.
Cash operating capex: 1.0603 / 0.0274 / 0.6116 / 0.2547 / 0.9625.
Reported FCF proxy: −1.4283 / −13.5178 / −10.5865 / −10.8900 / 30.2707.

Core EBIT after recurring finance fees, excluding deposit/other income, is approximately ₹24.6665 / 8.6510 / 5.8405 / 23.8360 / 9.8991 crore. The distinction matters: the model adds back borrowing interest, not every bank charge. FY2026 other income ₹0.4877 crore is chiefly deposit interest. Director remuneration and credit-loss expense remain operating costs, not discretionary add-backs that manufacture a high margin.

Three-year CFO/PAT is 42.95%; five-year is −6.92%. Deducting financing-classified cash interest reduces the three-year ratio to 10.71%. Three-year reported FCF is ₹8.7942 crore, but five-year FCF is −₹6.1519 crore, before that financing interest. FY2026 collection releases ₹61.9874 crore from receivables while payables consume ₹37.1071 crore; this explains the cash rebound without pretending it is recurring profit. Cash capex does not explain the earlier negative CFO.

Net receivables fall from ₹119.1242 to ₹55.5198 crore, yet gross amounts older than six months rise to ₹40.3500 crore, about 69.4% of gross receivables. The 6–12-month and 1–2-year buckets are ₹29.9149 and ₹3.6507 crore. Their stated ECL rates fall from 2%/5% to roughly 0.08%/1%; older buckets remain 30%/50%. Applying the old intermediate-age rates adds about ₹0.7204 crore provision before tax. This is a sensitivity, not a claim that the old rates are legally required. Deposit allowance also rises; the total ₹1.6170 crore credit-loss charge reconciles the receivable and deposit allowance increases. Subsequent customer-level receipts and the model-input rationale are still important.

Committed capital is approximately ₹26.45 / 48.71 / 64.86 / 96.44 / 73.91 crore over FY2022–26, retaining collateral and capital advances. Latest normalized NOPAT divided by average FY2025–26 capital is 8.70%; three-year incremental NOPAT/capital is 3.71%. These are cycle-level estimates, not manufacturing-project IRRs. The declining latest capital denominator does not justify an infinite or spectacular incremental return.

The opening-claim map includes all statutory, salary, bonus, trade and expense dues in broad WC; current and noncurrent unfunded gratuity of ₹0.0167/0.3477 crore are both included. Parent interest accrued ₹0.034 crore and unprovided tax demands ₹0.0305 crore settle once outside WC. Subsidiary current tax ₹0.0293 crore settles separately. Parent tax assets ₹1.6064 crore recover on a delayed schedule with a zero-recovery test, not a cross-entity legal offset. Reported margin deposits ₹9.7685 crore remain collateral, not free cash. Existing capital advances ₹1.6497 crore transfer to PPE without another payment. No duplicate dividend, benefit or acquisition claim is invented.

History is not silently restated: the later RHP FY2022 cash flow shows about ₹0.57 crore more tax paid and a similar increase in director financing than the older draft, with the same closing cash. The exact historical explanation is not independently established; the later audited restatement is used consistently. FY2024 statutory PAT exceeds the RHP figure by ₹0.0340 crore through disclosed depreciation/tax adjustments. These bounded presentation differences do not invalidate current audited aggregates. The FY2024 IPO added 5,040,000 shares; all current per-share values use 19,040,000 shares rather than the historical weighted-average EPS denominator.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹86.50, market value is ₹164.696 crore and current-share FY2026 P/E is about 32.3 times. Dated March net debt excluding pledged deposits gives enterprise value about ₹171.52 crore, around 17.2 times normalized operating EBITDA. This is a dated balance-sheet reference, not a verified October EV. Treating all bank deposits as free cash would understate operating capital and overstate distributable value.

The principal valuation is separate parent/subsidiary terminal NOPAT capitalization, with annual funding and exact terminal stub. Base parent/subsidiary multiples are 12/14; bear 9/9; bull 15/18. These are analytical ranges, not an observed matched-peer consensus. Parent intercompany lending earns estimated interest and recovers only after external subsidiary debt; founders receive 30% of residual subsidiary equity, not 30% of the entire listed parent. A guarantee shortfall falls to the parent.

Base terminal price ₹125.09, annual return 7.66%, 15% hurdle entry ₹62.19.
Bear terminal price ₹17.70, annual return -27.19%, hurdle entry ₹8.80.
Bull terminal price ₹298.47, annual return 28.11%, hurdle entry ₹148.39.

The base needs no hypothetical new parent shares. Terminal parent operating value, cash, debt, recoverable intercompany loan and 70% subsidiary residual reconcile to ₹238.18 crore over 1.904 crore shares. The minority value excluded is ₹7.37 crore. Annual parent and subsidiary cash identities are independently checked. Parent loan support is not counted both as group operating earnings and a free equity contribution.

Key sensitivities: parent WC at 90% gives about 2.46%; total new facility spend ₹20 crore gives 6.83%; ₹4 crore gives 8.02%; 15% financing cost gives 7.61%; zero recovery of tax assets gives 7.51%; ₹5/10 crore incremental asset losses give 7.11%/6.42%; no terminal subsidiary operating value gives 5.17%. Exact results and annual financing rows accompany the dossier. The ₹4 crore spending case crosses the mechanical 8% R boundary by very little; it does not establish a different precise economic fact.

At the base operating path, the 15% hurdle requires approximately 17.49 times parent terminal NOPAT rather than 12. A pure growth solution holding margins, WC, exit multiples and discounted equity issuance price fixed is especially misleading: the first tested crossing needs roughly 77.1% annual parent growth after FY2027 and more than ₹535 crore hypothetical new equity. That is a demonstration of dilution-heavy growth economics, not a credible forecast or the only way to meet the hurdle. Better margins, collections and renewal terms must be assessed jointly rather than assuming sales alone solve valuation.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that the apparent recovery is a liquidation of old receivables rather than a durable franchise improvement. New orders may again require long government credit, while the company funds devices, factory costs and related-party obligations before proving repeat demand. A lower opening debt balance can coexist with poor owner economics and limited realizable collateral.

The bear assumes parent sales only ₹55–74 crore, 9% parent EBIT, 90% WC, slower subsidiary uptake, ₹14 crore new facility spending and a ₹5 crore incremental asset loss. It values the shareholder at ₹17.70, about 79.5% below entry. The severe path combines lower/stagnant core activity, very weak margins, ₹20 crore facility spending and ₹15 crore asset impairment. Terminal equity is exhausted after financing and guarantee/loan priority. These are hypothetical linked stresses, not allegations that those losses already exist.

Impairment reduces opening recoverable WC, and replacement/foregone collection is funded once. There is no extra cash payment for a paper write-off. Current statutory/employee claims and collateral requirements are not omitted to make the stress appear funded. Nevertheless annual solvency does not prove every monthly cash peak is covered.

The thesis-break variable is repeatable cash profit after customer credit and project renewal, not hospital-sector growth. Material evidence that audited receivables are unreliable beyond the bounded loss tests, loss of critical OEM access, or refusal of necessary funding would invalidate the current conditional assessment and require a fresh gate decision.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold prices over five years require roughly 38.0% and 58.5% annual price growth. The strong bull reaches only about 3.45 times the dated entry price. Under fixed base margins, WC, debt caps, exit multiples and equity issuance price, scanning parent growth up to 80% annually does not reach either 5× or 10× because external funding dilutes the original shares. This is a bounded model test, not a mathematical proof that extraordinary outcomes are impossible.

A credible multibagger thesis would need materially better unit economics, faster cash conversion, a much more successful new product franchise and/or far less dilutive funding. None is verified today. Revenue growth, new capacity and national health spending are insufficient evidence by themselves.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Reconcile actual post-March collections with the remaining customer ledger. Baseline net receivables ₹55.52 crore and gross older-than-six-month balances ₹40.35 crore; obtain evidence rather than extrapolating the May aggregate claim.
2. Track ECL rates and realized losses by age bucket. Repeated ageing without collections matters more than a lower aggregate receivable total.
3. Separate awarded orders, bids, execution and cancellation. The ₹190 crore bid figure and ₹300–350 crore aspiration are not the starting backlog.
4. Verify SonoScape renewal before March 31, 2027, precise product exclusivity and commercial terms. Loss of access changes subsidiary assumptions.
5. Obtain a complete cost, ownership and financing schedule for the 45,000-square-foot facility. Compare actual spend with the ₹4–20 crore new-spend range and avoid crediting production before qualification.
6. Monitor parent versus subsidiary cash, loans and related-party terms. Founders own 30% directly; ensure listed-parent support is appropriately compensated and recoverable.
7. Track remuneration, related rent/interest and operating profitability together. Latest director compensation ₹3.682 crore consumes 72.2% of owner PAT.
8. Follow provider recovery, statutory-demand resolution and bank/book reconciliations, without counting already-paid GST or already-provided claims twice.
9. Track normalized CFO after financing interest, collateral growth and maintenance. A return to profitable sales growth with sustained negative cash would reinforce the cash-quality cap.
10. Refresh the 500-share lot, active cautions, spread and actual depth for the intended position. The reference 6.45-day liquidation estimate is not an execution promise.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final BQS 4.20 and IAS 2.85 place Aprameya in “Weak setup / value-trap risk” under the exact matrix. GQS 4.60 does not meet a high-quality compounder standard. This is not an Avoid—governance override or an accusation of misconduct; the weak conclusion follows unstable earnings, poor cycle-level cash/capital returns, downside and a dated price that does not meet the hurdle in the base.

Research action: keep on a recovery-verification watchlist rather than treating the device announcement or collection rebound as a completed investment case. The base 15% hurdle entry near ₹62 is conditional model arithmetic, not a recommended buy order or guaranteed floor. Lower price improves R, but durable reclassification also needs verified collections, new-product economics and fair subsidiary funding.

Substantial reasonable source review and financed scenarios are complete. Remaining cost, contract and collection uncertainties are explicit and bounded rather than hidden. The forecast remains uncertain even where the audited source hierarchy supports Medium evidence confidence.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Source hierarchy: the FY2026 signed annual report anchors current parent, consolidated and subsidiary figures; the FY2025 report supplies comparable earlier statutory data; the July 2024 RHP supersedes overlapping older draft figures; the September 2022 draft provides predecessor FY2020–21 context. The November presentation, May collection update, June agreement and August resolutions are dated management statements, not replacements for audited cash evidence. Exact URLs and page locators are in the source ledger.

Calculations use ₹ crore unless indicated. Reported CFO/PAT and FCF remain distinct from after-interest owner cash. Committed operating capital includes margin deposits, operating receivables, capital advances and liabilities; normalization removes treasury income and retains financing-service fees. Forecast investment, tax, debt, minority claims and share dilution are linked annually. Opening-claim treatment is itemized in the model audit. No arbitrary undisclosed score haircut follows the canonical factors.

The largest unresolved inputs are the current customer/order bridge, full facility cost and asset ownership, actual credit terms/draw timing, renewal and commercialization of device rights, and the related-party funding arrangement. They are not solved by the annual authorization ceiling. The provider claim is assigned no base recovery, and changing ECL rates are tested rather than asserted fraudulent. A live-execution check remains necessary.

Peer work establishes competition and business-model differences, not an unsupported current relative multiple. Government sector evidence supports demand but explicitly includes procurement delays. Assumed exit multiples, future margins, capital allocation and growth are analytical choices with disclosed ranges, not verified outcomes.

gates.reason: Reviewed controls, related transactions and audit reports do not substantiate serious minority abuse. High compensation and direct founder ownership in the subsidiary require continued commercial benchmarking; statutory delays and provider recovery are precisely scoped.

Audited parent/group/subsidiary statements reconcile after visual correction of extraction errors. Restatement differences are bounded and separated. Ageing, bank return differences and the provider claim are not declared resolved, but stress tests do not undermine the aggregate source hierarchy. A material new contradiction would require IAS NS.

Annual paths fund current claims, capital and WC through operating cash, disclosed facility caps and explicit hypothetical equity if needed. Full factory cost, loan draw conditions and monthly funding timing remain estimates. Subsidiary minority and guarantee claims are modeled, not omitted.

Sixty observed traded sessions and 500-share lot support a conditional reference-position test. Thin sessions, active concentration caution and unobserved executable spread/depth prevent a guaranteed-exit conclusion.

limitations: Current customer-level collection and order-book bridges are not available. The May total-collection claim is not treated as an additional cash receipt on top of March balances.

The complete 45,000-square-foot project budget, legal asset ownership after commissioning and final funding terms are unverified. Explicit capex/allocation ranges are assumptions, not approved contracts.
SonoScape agreement expires March 31, 2027 subject to renewal; no permanent exclusivity, Indian manufacturing technology licence or completed production approval is assumed.
The provider recovery and lower intermediate-age ECL rates remain open. Base excludes provider recovery and independently stresses receivable losses; no deliberate misconduct is inferred.
Future parent support to the 70%-owned subsidiary is modeled as priced debt with recovery priority. Actual related-party terms could differ and must be reviewed.
Live execution, current pledge quantities and a refreshed complete matched-peer valuation set were not independently verified. A dated absence of specified flags is not universal clearance.
next_steps: Obtain subsequent collections and the full government-customer ageing bridge, including the provider legal recovery.
Verify facility cost, asset ownership, commissioning and binding financing before crediting manufacturing margins.
Track renewal of the SonoScape contract and actual subsidiary orders, cash conversion and related-party financing.
Reconcile the next audited statements, current shareholder/pledge disclosures and live lot/depth before relying on the conditional valuation.

Director remuneration 3.682 crore is an other-expense item, not an unexplained excess over payroll. Founders each hold 15% of the subsidiary; the listed parent owns 70%. Related transactions and a 50 crore annual authorization need economic scrutiny.

Auditor reports short statutory-payment delays and small disputed income-tax/TDS demands. The GST input-credit reversal and provider recovery are already in the accounts. GOV.reason: Audited controls and explicit disclosures are useful, but founder remuneration absorbs 72.2% of owner PAT and founders personally own 30% of the growth subsidiary. Funding and commercial terms require minority scrutiny. This is a stewardship discount, not a finding of unlawful compensation or diversion.

MOAT.reason: Installation experience and OEM access help tender qualification. Technology is largely supplied by others, bids are competitive, one customer contributes 61.22%, and the new exclusive agreement renews annually. These do not establish durable pricing power.

REV.reason: The preselected five-year parent revenue window gives 16.12% CAGR, starting at 7. A one-point adjustment reflects the lumpy and deteriorating recent trajectory: three declines in the last four annual comparisons and 59.7% parent contraction in FY2026, despite strong first-half growth. Three-year decline and the FY2022 peak are shown, not selectively substituted for the preferred window. No further small-base or TAM adjustment is added.

DUR.reason: Hospital infrastructure and maintenance offer a real market, with named geographic access and a new device channel. Bid-to-order conversion, customer budgets, annual OEM renewal and factory qualification remain constraints. National spending is not secured company revenue.

CAP.reason: Latest normalized return on average committed operating capital is 8.70% and three-year incremental return 3.71%, below the 13–17% analytical range. FY2025 was much stronger, so this is weak cycle-level economics rather than a claim that every project destroys value. The new manufacturing investment has no demonstrated cohort return.

CASH.reason: Four of the last five years have negative CFO and cumulative five-year CFO/PAT is negative. FY2026 collection is genuine improvement, but old ageing, low after-interest realization and collateral demands mean the weakness is recurring rather than a single growth-capex event.

BAL.reason: Debt fell to 7.136 crore and dated credit access supports core modeled cash needs. However almost all reported bank deposits are collateral, parent free cash is very small at March, and the subsidiary guarantee and asset recoverability matter. The score does not assume all bank balances are distributable.

EXEC.reason: The older growth narrative has not translated into steady delivery:FY2026 sales contracted sharply andH2 profitability weakened. Collection normalization is a positive outcome, while the new facility, new-product commercialization and 300–350 crore aspirational order book remain unproven. This factor is about delivery against commitments, not a second cash-flow penalty.

EARN.reason: Owner PAT falls from 16.1161 to 5.102 crore, and the stronger first half was followed by a loss-making parent second half. Other income is not the main explanation; fixed overheads, business volume and credit provisions matter. A recovery is possible but is not already visible in comparable full-year earnings.

R.reason: The supported conditional base 7.6575% is 7.3425 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, exactly in R2. The lower-spend sensitivity barely crosses the 8% R3 boundary; that is model sensitivity, not a precise economic distinction.

D.reason: Bear terminal price 17.70 is about 79.5% below entry; severe terminal equity is exhausted even without assumed cash default. Low opening debt does not protect against stranded working capital, weaker margins and minority/loan recovery priority.

P.reason: At the base funded path,15% requires a 17.49-times parent terminal NOPAT multiple instead of 12, or materially better operating/cash assumptions. Fixed-price issuance makes a pure growth route extremely dilution-heavy. The price is not supported by the conservative recovery path, although the strong bull is possible.

L.reason: A 6.45-day theoretical exit starts in L5–6; use 5 then reduce one point for fewer-than 100-PAN caution, thin individual sessions, volatile high-low ranges and unobserved live depth. All 60 sessions actually traded; the generic SME caution is not misrepresented as zero-volume days.

opening_claim_audit.current_operating_claims: Parent trade payables ₹3.0584 crore, other financial liabilities ₹0.3801 crore excluding accrued interest, other current liabilities ₹1.3033 crore and current provisions ₹0.2252 crore are deducted in opening WC. These include statutory, salary, expense, bonus and current gratuity dues. Closing WC uses the same broad operating-liability scope.
opening_claim_audit.legacy_benefits: Parent unfunded gratuity ₹0.3644 crore, split ₹0.0167 current and ₹0.3477 noncurrent, is fully in WC. There are no plan assets to net. Future service cost is funded in forecast margins; no duplicate terminal benefit deduction. Leave obligation is reported paid at year-end.
opening_claim_audit.tax_interest: Parent ₹0.034 crore interest accrued is paid in FY2027, outside WC. The small ₹0.0039 crore MSME interest is conservatively treated as within this other-interest balance, not added twice; adding it independently would be an immaterial upper sensitivity. Unprovided income-tax/TDS demands ₹0.0305 crore are assumed paid once. Subsidiary current tax ₹0.0293 crore settles separately; parent tax assets are not legally netted across entities.
opening_claim_audit.tax_assets: Parent current ₹1.4282 crore and noncurrent ₹0.1782 crore income-tax assets are recovered in FY2028 and FY2030 respectively, with a zero-recovery sensitivity. Forecast current taxes remain cash-funded; these are distinct legacy recoveries.
opening_claim_audit.provider_recovery: The ₹1.3049 crore provider claim, including reversed GST credit and paid interest, is removed from normal opening WC and assigned no base cash recovery. A full-recovery alternative is shown. No new tax payment or cash write-off is charged for this already-recorded matter.
opening_claim_audit.capital: Existing ₹1.6497 crore capital advances transfer to parent building/PPE without another cash payment. New estimated plant spending is separately funded. No additional unmodeled acquisition/dividend liability was identified in the reviewed notes and current events; this is not an exhaustive future clearance.
opening_claim_audit.minority: Subsidiary is 70% owned by the listed parent and 15% each by the two founders. Future parent support is modeled as interest-bearing intercompany lending, not free equity for the minority. Terminal parent value includes recoverable loan plus 70% residual subsidiary equity; external debt has priority and any shortfall under the modeled guarantee falls to the parent.

assumption_basis.scope: Five-year investor horizon from October 19, 2026 to October 19, 2031. Operating bridge begins at the last audited March 2026 balance sheet, models full FY2027–31 and an exact 202/365 FY2032 stub. April–October changes are estimates, not a verified entry balance. Dated collection and loan announcements inform the bridge without being added as duplicate cash.
assumption_basis.sales: Base parent sales of ₹80/95/110/125/140/150 crore assume a recovery from FY2026 ₹54.75 crore, still below the FY2022 peak in the terminal year. New subsidiary sales of ₹3/6/10/15/20/24 crore are estimates, below the older ₹50 crore cumulative FY2029 aspiration. Bids and aspirational order books are not booked revenue. Bear/bull/severe paths vary both businesses explicitly.
assumption_basis.margins: Base parent EBIT margin is 15%, below FY2025–26 normalized operating margins after finance fees but above FY2024. Subsidiary margins rise from 10% to 14%, not its tiny initial-period margin extrapolated indefinitely. Ongoing director compensation, cash service costs, rent and bank operating fees remain in margins. External debt interest is separate. No dividend distribution is assumed.
assumption_basis.working_capital: Base parent broad WC is 65% of sales, close to the FY2025 ratio but much lower than the depressed FY2026 ratio. This is a collection-normalization assumption supported only partly by May management statements, not a proven new steady state. A 90% WC case and asset-loss stresses expose the risk. Subsidiary WC is 40% of sales. Impairments reduce opening recoverable WC and require replacement funding once, without a fictitious second cash payment.
assumption_basis.collateral: All ₹9.7685 crore bank deposits are reported as margin money. They remain operating collateral, at least the opening stock and otherwise 10% of parent annual sales. They are not terminal free cash. Interest on surplus cash is deliberately not assumed. A conditional release test is separate from the reference.
assumption_basis.capex: The issuer discloses a 45,000 sq. ft. facility but not a complete current project budget. The reference uses ₹10 crore new phased spending plus the already-paid ₹1.6497 crore advance, excluding existing land. This is an order-of-magnitude analytical budget, approximately ₹2,589 per sq. ft. including equipment, not a contractor quotation or approved cost. Allocation of 60% to parent building and 40% to subsidiary equipment is estimated. New-spend alternatives of ₹4 crore and ₹20 crore test the unresolved scope. Annual maintenance is 1% of parent sales and 4% of subsidiary sales, additional to construction. Buildings depreciate over an estimated 30 years; equipment over 10 years; no automatic full-building replacement after five years.
assumption_basis.funding: Base caps parent debt at the reported ₹32 crore cash-credit limit, without assuming the separately executed June ₹5.84 crore term facility has unrestricted revolving terms. A ₹37.84 crore alternative is shown. Subsidiary external capacity is ₹4 crore, subject to draw conditions. Blended external interest is 11%, tested at 15%; half-period draws/repayments and intercompany interest circularity are solved. Beyond capacity, hypothetical parent equity at a 30% discount with 5% issuance friction funds deficits. These are not promised credit or equity subscriptions.
assumption_basis.terminal: Parent operating NOPAT is capitalized at 12 times and subsidiary at 14 times in the base; bear uses 9/9 and bull 15/18. These are analytical ranges, not verified matched-peer trading multiples. Existing operating property and collateral are not added again. Minority participation, intercompany recoverability and external guarantee priority are explicit. Terminal shares match any modeled equity cash.
